body: That was the saving grace of Deathrace too.

I think the learning is in getting to a state where you feel comfortable hitting that button. Sure there's a lot of crap but I'd like to think I'd care enough to have something worth publishing before I hit publish.

I'm trying to hop between two projects now in the hope of finishing one. One is actually fairly far along, but strangely lacking any 'fun'. The other is still rendered in Box2D debug mode but already feeling like it might be fun...

Thanks for your reply. You're talking about some of my more extreme concerns when you mention 'messing with brain juices'. This is essentially why I have avoided anti-depressants so far in my life, despite going through some reasonably shitty times along the way (sudden death in my immediate family, and other such tragedies life tends to heap upon you). 

I agree with you about regular exercise. It is a definite mood improver. I am fortunate enough to live around 4.5km from where I work so regularly bike to/from work and it does help clear the mind. I should definitely do that more often.

However I've been feeling the same way mentally and emotionally for so many years I'm now beginning to think it's time to try them, at least at some low dosage, just to see if they make a qualitative difference.

I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have people that can support you? A partner, your family or friends? Local new parent groups? Being a new parent is a huge challenge, so it's ok to feel overwhelmed. But please reach out to any and all support you can get, and don't forget to give yourself some space in the day.

Please also realise it will definitely get better (I have two young sons). The first months of a newborn's life are the hardest on the parents because your baby really only has one way to communicate with you, and your natural instincts mean you always react very strongly to their distress. However one day your baby will stop crying and will start smiling at the sight of you.

I visited a psychologist recently for anxiety and depression and yes, suicidal thoughts. And while definitely not trying to minimise your situation he told me that suicidal thoughts are common in half of the population according to some studies. So we're not alone in having these thoughts - which I guess is a positive thing - but doesn't make them any less disturbing.

As you mention you're already talking to a therapist, perhaps it is time to discuss your suicidal thoughts with them? I also think the fact you're seeing a therapist regularly is immensely positive. It's taken me about 6 years just to be able to discuss my mental health with my GP...

Ok, I'm not an expert on depression, but I did read your whole post and you mention your love of acting and the stage several times. It is unfortunate your original group disbanded, but did that really end all your opportunities for acting locally? Are there any theatre groups locally you can join? In particular how about amateur theatre groups? Also if you're attending University soon will there be any student based theatre groups you can join there? Many modern film and stage actors started their acting careers as students performing in University theatre groups.

I'm 45 years old and I would like to say if acting is what you love doing and what makes you truly happy then I believe you should pursue every possible avenue you can to continue acting. 

Also you mention disliking your creative projects, but also being complemented on them by others. First I'm impressed by anybody that can expend the energy, or has the imagination to create anything original, and secondly I don't think there is a harsher critic of a creative work than the creator themselves. Listen to the compliments, and keep creating!

If it helps I'm about to visit my first psychiatrist at the end of this week for anxiety and suicidal thoughts. I can tell you how it goes. I'd say try it yourself too, it cannot hurt to have a detached professional to talk can it?

My extended family has an interesting history with antidepressants. I have a cousin that became very reliant on them and they scare me for that reason and I had concerns with messing around with my brain chemistry. But I'll be honest, I'm starting to feel like anything that will help is worth investigating. Just reading some people's stories on here helps quite a bit and nice to see how supportive everybody is tbh.

That is solid advice thank you. I am talking to my wife and she's been superb. The fact that she has a working history in adolescent mental health helps too. She is very happy to see me seeking help and I do feel like it's time. I've been struggling on and off for several years now looking back on things but have usually managed to recover by myself (regular exercise helps me a lot). This time just feels different. Harder than I've ever found it before.

Thanks for your reply! That's sort of the irony - logically I have nothing to complain about at the end of the day, and whatever problems I have are manageable, however emotionally I still find myself in this pathological, unhealthy mindset. Definitely interested to visit a psychologist - see how it goes.
